thesis.claim: Raiders that pool their stakes take hold where lone raiders cannot. In B2's worlds played on, at iterations 5,000 and 10,000, where patches of 5% of lone raiders took hold in none of 30 plantings, patches of 5% of crew raiders — raiders that stake on the weakest stranger next door no richer than themselves, every token of it a revolution token, so that raiders bordering the same stranger become one mob — take hold in at least 5 of the same 30 plantings.
thesis.why: In Experiment 30 the lone raider's door closed because the patches it started from grew poor: it needs three tokens to take even a neighbour of one, and by iteration 5,000 a patch held two tokens an agent. In that game a node goes to the largest single stake, the holder's own counting one and a half times, unless revolutionaries together outweigh it. Two raiders of two tokens, each staking one as a revolution token, take a stranger of one token that neither could take alone. Raiders that each see the same stranger as the weakest next door join without any message. A world of many small agents shuts out lone raiders, not crews: if that is so, the poorer the world, the more a group is worth.
thesis.confirm: At least 5 of the 30 crew plantings at 5,000 and 10,000 take hold: alive after 300 iterations, more than the patch began with, and more than the control planted in the same place.
thesis.refute: Four or fewer take hold: pooling stakes does not open the door, and the chapter says what the crews met instead.
